label: Self-designed process
summary: A self-designed process is a personal workflow that a conversation designer working alone builds for themselves, since no standardised template exists for the role. It serves a dual purpose: helping the designer keep track of different responsibilities and switch deliberately between roles, and making the work legible to colleagues and stakeholders. It is something you sketch out yourself rather than inherit from a team or organisation.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike frames the self-designed process as a practical survival tool for the lone conversation designer. She recommends visualising it explicitly, not just for personal clarity but as a communication device so others can understand what you actually do. She pairs it with the idea of a self-imposed release rhythm, treating the two together as a way to impose structure when no external structure is provided.
open_questions: What a good self-designed process actually looks like in practice is left open — Maaike gestures at sketching roles but gives no concrete template.
How the process should evolve as the field of conversation design itself matures is not addressed.
